label: Superset

kerberos._principalValuePath: The chart's kinit sidecar derives <serviceLabel>-<namespace>@<realm> when this value is empty; KDPS shortens primaries above the FreeIPA 32-char limit when it issues the keytab, so the issued name is pinned here or kinit fails with 'Keytab contains no suitable keys'.

variables.comment: Default Trino catalog for the Superset connection URL (trino://host:port/<catalog>). Defaults to 'hive'; other catalogs remain reachable via catalog.schema.table.
variables.name: trinoCatalog

variables.comment: How Superset authenticates TO the Trino coordinator, matching the security profile Trino was deployed with (none / tls / ldap / kerberos). Impersonation is applied for ALL of these — see the import_datasources_trino.yaml bindings.
variables.name: trinoAuthMode

variables.comment: true when Trino has no client auth (plain HTTP). URL only, plus impersonation.
variables.name: trinoModeNone

variables.comment: true when Trino is HTTPS with no login (TLS transport only). connect_args http_scheme=https + verify against the mounted CA, plus impersonation.
variables.name: trinoModeTls

variables.comment: true when Trino uses LDAP/AD password auth. Superset authenticates with a service account (BasicAuthentication over HTTPS) and impersonates the logged-in user via the Trino session user.
variables.name: trinoModeLdap

variables.comment: true when Trino uses Kerberos (SPNEGO). Superset authenticates with the pod's ccache (KerberosAuthentication over HTTPS) and impersonates the logged-in user.
variables.name: trinoModeKerberos

variables.comment: true when Trino uses OIDC/OAUTH2. Superset presents a Keycloak service JWT (client-credentials, kept fresh by the trino-jwt sidecar and read per request by the kdps_file_jwt custom auth) over HTTPS and impersonates the logged-in user. Requires the Trino JWT authenticator (chart >= 1.43.7).
variables.name: trinoModeOidc

variables.comment: HS2 transport mode (http/binary) resolved from the selected KDPS context (managed: hive-site hive.server2.transport.mode; external: typed). Drives the hive:// vs impala:// driver choice below. Unset when Hive is disabled.
variables.name: hiveTransportMode

variables.comment: true ONLY when the resolved transport is binary → use the PyHive hive:// driver.
variables.name: hiveModeBinary

variables.comment: true for anything that is NOT binary (http / all / unresolved): the Hive datasource uses PyHive over HTTP(S). Safe default when a context does not report a transport mode.
variables.name: hiveModeHttp

variables.comment: Scheme of HiveServer2's HTTP endpoint (https/http), from the context; override with hiveDb.scheme (Knox is always https).
variables.name: hiveScheme

variables.comment: true only when the operator turned dynamic role mapping ON — gates the binding below.
variables.name: dynamicRoleOn

bindings.name: ingress-setup
bindings._description: Writes the canonical ingress shape every KDPS chart accepts. The `hosts[]` entry uses the rich object form `{host, paths[]}` so OpenMetadata- and Trino-style charts work out of the box; the Superset chart's template was made shape-tolerant (accepts string OR object) in chart >= 0.12.25.

bindings.name: openshift-route-allowlist
bindings._description: On OpenShift the chart copies ingress.annotations onto its Route; some clusters refuse a Route without this router annotation.

bindings.name: ingress-nginx-tuning
bindings._description: Backslash-escaped dots in the leaf key — the UI binding engine (bindings.ts:pathToParts) treats backslash-dot as a literal dot so the rendered values look like `ingress.annotations: { "nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size": "..." }`.

bindings.name: ingress-setup
bindings._description: Writes the canonical ingress shape every KDPS chart accepts. The `hosts[]` entry uses the rich object form `{host, paths[]}` so OpenMetadata- and Trino-style charts work out of the box; the Superset chart's template was made shape-tolerant (accepts string OR object) in chart >= 0.12.25.

bindings.name: ingress-nginx-tuning
bindings._description: Backslash-escaped dots in the leaf key — the UI binding engine (bindings.ts:pathToParts) treats backslash-dot as a literal dot so the rendered values look like `ingress.annotations: { "nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size": "..." }`.

bindings.comment: Trino database (auth=none): plain HTTP, no login. Superset connects over the trino:// SQLAlchemy dialect and, because impersonate_user is true, sets the Trino session user to the logged-in Superset user (TrinoEngineSpec.update_impersonation_config) — so Ranger authorises each person individually. Written to import_datasources_trino.yaml (NOT import_datasources.yaml) so it never collides with the Platform Hive database; the chart bootstrap imports every import_datasources*.yaml. Fires only when a Trino host is set AND the auth mode is 'none'.
bindings.name: superset-trino-datasource-none

template.import_datasources_trino.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Trino
  sqlalchemy_uri: trino://${trinoHost}:${trinoPort}/${trinoCatalog}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {"source": "superset-kdps"}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Trino database (auth=tls): HTTPS transport, no client login. connect_args forces http_scheme=https and verifies against the CA the chart mounts at /etc/security/truststore/ca.crt (requires the Superset TLS truststore to be configured). Impersonation as above. Fires when a Trino host is set AND the auth mode is 'tls'.
bindings.name: superset-trino-datasource-tls

template.import_datasources_trino.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Trino
  sqlalchemy_uri: trino://${trinoHost}:${trinoPort}/${trinoCatalog}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {"source": "superset-kdps", "http_scheme": "https", "verify": "/etc/security/truststore/ca.crt"}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Trino database (auth=ldap): HTTPS + Basic auth with an LDAP/AD service account, expressed as encrypted_extra {auth_method: basic} (TrinoEngineSpec.update_params_from_encrypted_extra builds trino.auth.BasicAuthentication and forces https). Queries still run as the logged-in user via impersonation — the service account only needs impersonation rights on Trino (Ranger). Fires when a Trino host is set AND the auth mode is 'ldap'.
bindings.name: superset-trino-datasource-ldap

template.import_datasources_trino.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Trino
  sqlalchemy_uri: trino://${trinoHost}:${trinoPort}/${trinoCatalog}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {"source": "superset-kdps", "verify": "/etc/security/truststore/ca.crt"}}}'
  encrypted_extra: '{"auth_method": "basic", "auth_params": {"username": "${trinoSvcUser}", "password": "${trinoSvcPassword}"}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Trino database (auth=kerberos): HTTPS + SPNEGO, expressed as encrypted_extra {auth_method: kerberos} → trino.auth.KerberosAuthentication using the pod's krb5.conf and the ccache the kinit sidecar keeps at KRB5CCNAME, verifying against the mounted CA. Impersonation sets the Trino session user to the logged-in user. Fires when a Trino host is set AND the auth mode is 'kerberos'.
bindings.name: superset-trino-datasource-kerberos

template.import_datasources_trino.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Trino
  sqlalchemy_uri: trino://${trinoHost}:${trinoPort}/${trinoCatalog}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {"source": "superset-kdps"}}}'
  encrypted_extra: '{"auth_method": "kerberos", "auth_params": {"config": "/etc/krb5.conf", "service_name": "trino", "ca_bundle": "/etc/security/truststore/ca.crt"}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Trino database (auth=oidc): HTTPS + a Keycloak service JWT. encrypted_extra auth_method=kdps_file_jwt selects the custom auth registered in superset_config.py (the chart's ALLOWED_EXTRA_AUTHENTICATIONS), which reads a fresh token per request from the file the trino-jwt sidecar refreshes; TrinoEngineSpec forces http_scheme=https for any encrypted_extra auth. The second target flips trinoJwt.enabled=true so the chart runs the refresh sidecar (it reuses the Superset OIDC client Secret — that client must have service accounts enabled). Impersonation runs each query as the logged-in user. Requires Trino chart >= 1.43.7 (JWT authenticator). Fires when a Trino host is set AND the auth mode is 'oidc'.
bindings.name: superset-trino-datasource-oidc

template.import_datasources_trino.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Trino
  sqlalchemy_uri: trino://${trinoHost}:${trinoPort}/${trinoCatalog}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {"source": "superset-kdps", "verify": "/etc/security/truststore/ca.crt"}}}'
  encrypted_extra: '{"auth_method": "kdps_file_jwt", "auth_params": {}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Hive over PyHive, binary transport + Kerberos (SASL/GSSAPI with the pod's ccache). Superset impersonates the logged-in user through hive.server2.proxy.user, so Ranger authorizes and audits the END USER; the service principal only needs hadoop.proxyuser rights on the cluster.
bindings.name: superset-hive-datasource-kerberos-binary

template.import_datasources.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Hive
  sqlalchemy_uri: hive://${hiveHostPort}/default
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {"auth": "KERBEROS", "kerberos_service_name": "hive"}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Hive over PyHive, HTTP(S) transport + Kerberos (SPNEGO, ODP-patched PyHive: requests transport, HS2 auth cookie, http_path for Knox). Same end-user impersonation via hive.server2.proxy.user. ssl_cert=none skips certificate verification; 'required' verifies against the pod's CA bundle.
bindings.name: superset-hive-datasource-kerberos-http

template.import_datasources.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Hive
  sqlalchemy_uri: hive+${hiveScheme}://${hiveHostPort}/default?auth=KERBEROS&kerberos_service_name=hive&http_path=${hiveHttpPath}&ssl_cert=${hiveSslCert}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Hive over PyHive, binary transport + LDAP: the connection authenticates with the operator's LDAP service account and impersonates the logged-in user (hive.server2.proxy.user).
bindings.name: superset-hive-datasource-ldap-binary

template.import_datasources.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Hive
  sqlalchemy_uri: hive://${hiveLdapUser}:${hiveLdapPassword}@${hiveHostPort}/default?auth=LDAP
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Hive over PyHive, HTTP(S) transport + LDAP/Basic (direct HS2 in LDAP mode, or through Knox with http_path=gateway/<topology>/hive). Service account authenticates, the logged-in user is impersonated.
bindings.name: superset-hive-datasource-ldap-http

template.import_datasources.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Hive
  sqlalchemy_uri: hive+${hiveScheme}://${hiveLdapUser}:${hiveLdapPassword}@${hiveHostPort}/default?auth=BASIC&http_path=${hiveHttpPath}&ssl_cert=${hiveSslCert}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Hive over PyHive, binary transport, unsecured HiveServer2 (hive.server2.authentication=NONE). Still impersonates the logged-in user so per-user authorization applies where configured.
bindings.name: superset-hive-datasource-none-binary

template.import_datasources.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Hive
  sqlalchemy_uri: hive://${hiveHostPort}/default?auth=NONE
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.comment: Hive over PyHive, HTTP(S) transport, unsecured HiveServer2 (authentication NONE).
bindings.name: superset-hive-datasource-none-http

template.import_datasources.yaml:
databases:
- database_name: Platform Hive
  sqlalchemy_uri: hive+${hiveScheme}://${hiveHostPort}/default?auth=NONE&http_path=${hiveHttpPath}&ssl_cert=${hiveSslCert}
  extra: '{"engine_params": {"connect_args": {}}}'
  impersonate_user: true
  allow_run_async: true
  allow_ctas: false
  allow_cvas: false
  tables: []

bindings.name: superset-secret-key
bindings.comment: extraSecretEnv, not extraEnv: the chart puts it in the <fullname>-env Secret the pods read through envFrom, so the key does not show in the pod specs (anyone allowed to read Deployments could sign a session cookie or decrypt the stored database passwords with it). Superset still reads SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY, so the key, and what it encrypted, are unchanged.

Dynamic role mapping: fires only when the operator toggled it on. Sets global.security.dynamicRoleFromGroup=true (the chart maps it to SECURITY_DYNAMIC_ROLE_FROM_GROUP) and, when provided, the role-name pattern. Superset then grants any role whose name matches an IdP group at login — no restart. Requires superset chart >= 0.12.43.
bindings.name: superset-dynamic-role-mapping

form.name: releaseName
form.label: release name
form.validationHint: Use at most 53 lower-case letters, digits, '-' and '.', starting and ending with a letter or digit (Helm's rule for release names).

form.name: trinoConnection
form.label: Connect to Trino
form.help: Pick a running Trino to fill its host and port below.

form.name: ui_trino_host
form.label: Trino host
form.help: Filled when you pick a Trino above. Blank: no Trino connection.
form.helpMore: Set it by hand for a Trino deployed outside KDPS.

form.name: ui_trino_port
form.label: Trino port
form.help: Trino coordinator port, filled when you pick a Trino above.
form.helpMore: 8080 for plain HTTP; the HTTPS port when Trino uses TLS, LDAP or OIDC.

form.name: ui_trino_auth_mode
form.label: Trino authentication
form.help: Match the security profile Trino was deployed with.
form.helpMore:
Superset always runs queries as the logged-in user, so Ranger authorizes each person whatever the mode.
OIDC uses a Keycloak service token (the Superset OIDC client needs service accounts enabled) and Trino's JWT authenticator (Trino chart 1.43.7+). A Trino deployed by KDPS accepts only tokens minted for it, and KDPS adds its audience to Superset's tokens; another Trino must accept the audience your identity provider sets.

form.name: ui_trino_catalog
form.label: Default Trino catalog
form.help: Default catalog of the Trino connection, e.g. hive or iceberg. Required.
form.helpMore: Without it Trino rejects SQL Lab queries that pick a schema ('Schema is set but catalog is not'). Other catalogs stay reachable as catalog.schema.table.

form.name: ui_trino_svc_user
form.label: Trino service username
form.help: Account Superset signs in to Trino with; it only needs to impersonate.
form.helpMore: Queries still run as the logged-in user.

form.name: ui_trino_svc_password
form.label: Trino service password
form.help: Password of the Trino account above. Kept in a Secret (chart 0.12.49+).

form.name: ui_trino_ranger_service
form.label: Trino Ranger service name
form.help: Blank for a Trino deployed by KDPS: its Ranger repository is found.
form.helpMore: Set it when the Trino's Ranger repository has another name, e.g. an externally managed Trino.

form.name: ui_trino_oidc_principal
form.label: Trino service principal (for the impersonation grant)
form.help: Principal Trino sees for Superset's token, to grant it 'impersonate'.
form.helpMore:
Usually service-account-<client-id> for a Keycloak client-credentials token (Trino's jwt.principal-field, default preferred_username). KDPS then grants it 'impersonate' on Trino user '*' in Ranger.
Left blank, add that Ranger policy yourself: without it, Trino refuses every Superset query.

fields.name: hiveDb.enabled
fields.label: Connect to platform Hive
fields.help: Adds a Superset connection to the context's HiveServer2.
fields.helpMore: Authentication and transport follow the context; queries run as the logged-in user (hive.server2.proxy.user), so Ranger authorizes and audits each person.

fields.name: hiveDb.hostPort
fields.label: HiveServer2 host:port
fields.help: Delivered by KDPS from the selected Platform Context. Toggle Override only to point at a specific HiveServer2.

fields.name: hiveDb.authMode
fields.label: Hive authentication
fields.help: From the platform context: kerberos, ldap or none.

fields.name: hiveDb.transportMode
fields.label: HS2 transport mode
fields.help: From the platform context. Override only to force a driver.
fields.helpMore: binary uses the PyHive hive:// driver; http (or unknown) uses impyla impala:// over HTTP.

fields.name: hiveDb.scheme
fields.label: HS2 HTTP scheme
fields.help: http or https for HiveServer2 over HTTP (Knox: https). From the context.

fields.name: hiveDb.httpPath
fields.label: HS2 HTTP path
fields.help: HTTP transport only. 'cliservice' for a direct HiveServer2; through Knox use the topology path, e.g. gateway/default/hive.

fields.name: hiveDb.sslCert
fields.label: Verify HS2 TLS certificate

options.label: Verify against the pod's CA bundle

fields.help: HTTPS only: check the HiveServer2 or Knox certificate.
fields.helpMore: Verify uses the CA bundle the chart mounts; the certificate must chain to it.

fields.name: hiveDb.ldapUser
fields.label: Hive LDAP service account
fields.help: LDAP account Superset signs in to Hive with (LDAP Hive only).
fields.helpMore: Queries run as the logged-in user, so the account needs hadoop.proxyuser rights on the cluster.

fields.name: hiveDb.ldapPassword
fields.label: Hive LDAP service account password
fields.help: Password of the LDAP account above. Kept in a Secret (chart 0.12.49+).
fields.helpMore: Superset also encrypts it in its metadata database.

fields.name: hiveDb.externalKeytabSecret
fields.label: External Superset service keytab Secret
fields.help: Secret with Superset's keytab from another realm. Blank: KDPS issues it.
fields.helpMore:
Only for an external context with a Kerberos Hive whose KDC KDPS cannot reach (no KDC account on the context). The Secret, in the release namespace, holds key 'keytab'; set its principal below.
kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic superset-keytab --from-file=keytab=./superset.keytab

fields.name: hiveDb.externalKeytabPrincipal
fields.label: External Superset service principal
fields.help: Principal of the keytab above. Blank: the Secret's 'principal' key.

fields.name: ingress.enabled
fields.label: Enable Ingress
fields.help: Expose the service through an Ingress (a Route on OpenShift).
fields.helpMore: Required with an authentication profile (OIDC, LDAP over TLS): sign-in needs a public hostname and HTTPS.

fields.name: ingress.ingressClassName
fields.label: Ingress class
fields.help: Ingress class name (e.g. 'nginx', 'openshift-default'). Leave empty for the default controller.

fields.name: ingress.host
fields.label: Hostname (DNS)
fields.help: Public DNS name the ingress controller will route. e.g. service.example.com.

fields.name: ingress.path
fields.label: HTTP path
fields.help: Base path for the Ingress (usually '/').

fields.name: ingress.tlsMode
fields.label: TLS mode
fields.help: Where the service's TLS certificate comes from.
fields.helpMore:
Sign via cert-manager: recommended when cert-manager is installed (renews automatically).
Sign with Company CA: a CA uploaded under Security → Certificate Authorities.
Sign with Ambari Internal CA: for tests, browsers warn.
Modes whose system is not installed are hidden. TLS is required with an authentication profile.
On Upgrade/Config this starts on 'Keep current certificate' (or 'None' for plain HTTP). Pick another mode only to replace the certificate; you are asked to confirm, and a Secret kept by cert-manager or an external store is never overwritten.

options.label: Source from external Secret store (Vault, ESO)
None (HTTP only — not allowed with auth)

fields.name: ingress.tlsSecret
fields.label: Existing TLS Secret name
fields.help: Name of a kubernetes.io/tls Secret already present in the release namespace. The chart references it via ingress.tls[].secretName.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.cert
fields.label: TLS certificate (PEM, leaf + chain)
fields.help: Paste the full chain (leaf first). Saved as tls.crt in the new Secret.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.key
fields.label: TLS private key (PEM)
fields.help: Paste the private key matching the certificate above. Saved as tls.key.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.secretName
fields.label: Target Secret name
fields.help: Secret created from the uploaded certificate. Blank: <release>-ingress-tls.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.caName
fields.label: Company CA
fields.help: Company CA that signs the service's certificate.
fields.helpMore: KDPS signs the certificate itself: the CA key never goes to the release's cluster. Upload CAs under Security → Certificate Authorities.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: How long the minted leaf certificate is valid. Capped server-side at 825 (CA/Browser Forum baseline).

fields.name: ingress.certManager.issuerName
fields.label: ClusterIssuer
fields.help: cert-manager issuer that signs and renews the certificate.
fields.helpMore: KDPS writes a Certificate before the install; cert-manager creates the Secret and renews it before it expires.

fields.name: ingress.certManager.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: Validity in days. Translated to durationHours on the Certificate resource. cert-manager renews at duration/6 before expiry.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.secretStoreName
fields.label: SecretStore
fields.help: Pick an external-secrets SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore. Typically Vault-backed for TLS leaves (PKI mount).

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.remoteKey
fields.label: Remote key / path
fields.help: Path of the certificate in the external store.
fields.helpMore: Vault PKI: pki/issue/<role>. Vault KV: secret/data/tls/<name>. AWS Secrets Manager: the secret's name.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.refreshInterval
fields.label: Refresh interval
fields.help: ESO refresh cadence. e.g. '1h', '15m', '0' (no periodic refresh).

fields.name: ingress.route.ipWhitelist
fields.label: Allowed source IPs (OpenShift Route)
fields.help: Source IPs or CIDRs allowed to reach the Route, space separated. Blank: all.
fields.helpMore: OpenShift only, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 172.16.20.0/24. Set it when the cluster requires the haproxy.router.openshift.io/ip_whitelist annotation on every Route.

fields.name: ingressTuning
fields.label: Ingress tuning (nginx)

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBufferSize
fields.label: proxy-buffer-size
fields.help: nginx proxy-buffer-size. Blank: the chart's default.
fields.helpMore: 16k under OIDC, else nginx's default (4k/8k). Raise it on 502 'upstream sent too big header' after sign-in.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBuffersNumber
fields.label: proxy-buffers-number
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers-number. Total response buffers = number × size.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBusyBuffersSize
fields.label: proxy-busy-buffers-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-busy-buffers-size. Should be ≥ proxy-buffer-size and ≤ total buffer capacity.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBodySize
fields.label: proxy-body-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size. Maximum request body the proxy accepts (e.g. '64m'). Bump for large uploads / file imports.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyReadTimeout
fields.label: proxy-read-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout. Bump for long-running queries (Trino, Superset). Default 60.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyConnectTimeout
fields.label: proxy-connect-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout. Time the proxy waits when opening a connection to the backend pod.
Advanced nginx settings: usually leave blank.
fields.helpMore: Override them for large OAuth headers, long-running queries or big uploads.

fields.name: superset.secretKey
fields.label: SECRET_KEY
fields.help: Signs sessions and encrypts stored database passwords. Required.
fields.helpMore:
Kept in a Secret. On an upgrade it holds the key the release runs with: keep it, or the stored database passwords can no longer be decrypted.
Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 42

fields.name: superset.openstreetmapServerUrl
fields.label: OpenStreetMap Server URL
fields.help: URL of the OpenStreetMap server used by Superset. Leave blank to keep Superset's default map tiles.

fields.name: supersetWorker.concurrency
fields.label: Worker processes
fields.help: Celery worker processes for SQL Lab, reports and alerts.
fields.helpMore: Blank, Celery starts one per CPU of the node: dozens on a large node, and a worker killed for memory. Allow about 400 MiB of worker memory per process. Chart 0.12.52+.

fields.name: supersetWorker.resources.limits.memory
fields.label: Worker memory limit
fields.help: Memory limit of the Celery worker pod, e.g. 2Gi for 4 worker processes, 4Gi for 8.

fields.name: security.adminUsers
fields.label: Admin users (comma-separated)
fields.help: Optional list of Superset usernames that should be granted the Admin role.

fields.name: security.adminGroups
fields.label: Admin groups (comma-separated)
fields.help: Optional list of IdP groups to map to the Admin role (e.g., LDAP/OIDC groups).

fields.name: security.dynamicRoleFromGroup
fields.label: Dynamic role mapping from IdP groups
fields.help: Grants, at each login, the roles named like the user's groups.
fields.helpMore: Groups come from LDAP, AD or OIDC; roles are looked up live, so a role created in Superset applies at the next login, without a restart. Restrict them with the pattern below.

fields.name: security.dynamicRolePattern
fields.label: Auto-grant role name pattern (regex)
fields.help: Regex a role name must match to be granted, e.g. ^ad_.
fields.helpMore: Recommended in production, so a directory group cannot match a sensitive role such as Admin. Blank: any role named like a group.

fields.name: global.security.auth.localLoginFallback
fields.label: Break-glass local sign-in
fields.help: Lets the local 'admin' sign in when the directory or IdP is down.
fields.helpMore: On the login form (LDAP, AD) or at /login/local (OIDC). While on, anyone reaching Superset can try local passwords: leave it off otherwise. The password is in the Secret <release>-superset-admin. Chart 0.12.50+.

form.name: openshiftOptions
form.label: OpenShift
form.help: OpenShift-specific options. Only shown when KDPS detects the cluster is OpenShift.

fields.name: runAsUser
fields.label: Run pods as a specific UID (optional)
fields.help: Leave blank: OpenShift picks a UID from the project's range.
fields.helpMore: Set a UID only if you must pin one. It must fall inside the namespace's openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range annotation, or admission rejects the pods.

description: Modern data exploration and visualisation platform. Build dashboards and charts directly from your data warehouse.

retiredValues._comment: Values an earlier version of this definition wrote, removed from the values of every deploy (wizard upgrades and redeploys without the wizard alike).
retiredValues.extraEnv.SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY: The SECRET_KEY now goes to extraSecretEnv: left in extraEnv, it would still show in the pod specs.
retiredValues.superset-env/SUPERSET_ADMIN_PASSWORD: The wizard no longer asks for an administrator password, which the chart never read: KDPS generates it into the Secret <release>-superset-admin.

secretChartVersions._comment: Chart 0.12.49 keeps the datasource import files (extraConfigs) in a Secret and passes the security profile's bind password to the pods through secretKeyRef; an older chart puts them in a ConfigMap or a plain environment variable. A wizard deploy that carries one of them with an older chart is refused; a resync or a security refresh is warned in its operation log.

ui_trino_svc_password.label: the Trino service-account password of the datasource import file

hiveDb.ldapPassword.label: the Hive LDAP service-account password of the datasource import file

global.security.auth.ldap.bindPassword.label: the security profile's LDAP bind password

global.security.auth.ad.bindPassword.label: the security profile's Active Directory bind password

generatedSecrets.comment: The local administrator the init job creates. Never admin/admin: a random password generated once and kept in this Secret, which the release keeps after an uninstall. resetPassword is true from the deploy that generates it until a deploy succeeds, so an administrator created before (with the chart default admin/admin) gets it too, even when the first deploy fails or is refused.
generatedSecrets.label: the Superset administrator password
generatedSecrets.notice: Superset administrator 'admin': its password is in the Secret {{namespace}}/{{secretName}}. Read it with: {{readCommand}}. With a security profile attached, this local account signs in only while 'Break-glass local sign-in' (Administrative users/groups) is on.

generatedSecrets.comment: The bundled PostgreSQL keeps the passwords it was initialized with: a release installed before keeps those its chart stored in <release>-postgresql, or, when an uninstall deleted that Secret, the user password the chart set for every release (superset). Superset never signs in as postgres: that password is generated when it cannot be found.
generatedSecrets.label: the passwords of the Superset PostgreSQL database

securityCoupling.unauthenticatedExposure: Superset then signs users in with its local accounts only, starting with the administrator this deploy creates: your directory and single sign-on are not used, and that one password guards every database connection Superset holds.

sizing._comment: Sizes offered at step 3 of the wizard. A size fills the listed form fields; M is the fields' defaults. The fields are edited in the sizing dialog instead of the form.

gitOpsSecretReferences._comment: A GitOps profile commits the values to Git: each secret goes to a Secret of the release namespace, which the values name (StackServiceDef.gitOpsSecretReferences).

gitOpsSecretReferences.label: the security profile's bind password or OIDC client secret
